Rule_Name: GPU Compute Metric Must Match Workload
Rule_Description: DSS must select a performance metric that represents the workload objective before comparing candidate GPUs.
Inputs: Workload type; target metric; candidate performance
Output_Decision: Use the same metric family for candidate-vs-target comparison
Page_Section_Table: Training Scenarios & Metrics; Inference Datacenter Scenarios
Evidence: MLPerf uses scenario/model-specific performance metrics rather than a single universal GPU metric.
Applicability: All GPU workload sizing.
Limitations: A theoretical FLOPS number alone may not represent application performance.

Rule_Description: When a workload uses a supported precision, DSS should use the corresponding precision-specific catalogue performance field when available rather than substituting another precision's peak value.
Inputs: Workload precision; candidate GPU precision performance
Output_Decision: Use matching precision performance evidence; otherwise require benchmark evidence or mark field unavailable
Exact_Source_Title: Train With Mixed Precision / GPU Catalogue
Page_Section_Table: Mixed Precision Training; GPU catalogue header
Evidence: NVIDIA documents precision-dependent Tensor Core behavior; the DSS catalogue stores several precision-specific compute fields.
Applicability: Only where the candidate GPU and software stack support the precision.
Limitations: INT8/INT4 may not have dedicated catalogue compute fields; do not invent them.

Rule_Description: For INT8 or INT4 inference, DSS must not substitute FP16/BF16/FP8 performance values unless the source explicitly establishes comparability.
Inputs: Selected precision; candidate benchmark; candidate precision support
Condition: Selected precision is INT8 or INT4
Output_Decision: Use precision-specific benchmark/vendor evidence or mark performance unavailable
Page_Section_Table: Benchmark context; Tensor_Performance field
Evidence: Benchmark results are scenario/model-specific and the catalogue does not provide a dedicated universal INT4 performance field.
Applicability: Inference workloads using INT8/INT4.
Limitations: No universal mapping from another precision to INT8/INT4 performance.

Rule_Name: Candidate GPU Performance Must Be Comparable
Rule_Description: Candidate GPU performance evidence must match the target workload's model, precision, batch/load, software and benchmark context closely enough for comparison.
Inputs: Model; precision; batch; load; GPU; software/runtime; benchmark version; metric
Output_Decision: Use benchmark result; otherwise downgrade confidence and avoid direct equivalence
Exact_Source_Title: MLPerf Training / MLPerf Inference / Triton Performance Analyzer
Page_Section_Table: MLPerf benchmarking; Triton measurement modes
Evidence: MLPerf and Triton measure performance under defined workload/system/load configurations.
Applicability: Comparable benchmark configurations.
Limitations: A benchmark from a different model/load/precision cannot automatically become a universal requirement.

Rule_Description: One GPU is sufficient only when the workload fits the usable GPU memory and the measured/validated performance on that GPU satisfies the workload target.
Inputs: Required memory; usable memory; candidate performance; workload target
Condition: Memory feasible AND performance target satisfied
Output_Decision: Select one GPU as resource-sufficient; otherwise evaluate additional GPUs
Page_Section_Table: GPU memory and precision performance fields; existing feasibility and target rules
Evidence: Combines existing memory/performance constraints without duplicating them.
Applicability: Single-GPU candidate evaluation.
Limitations: Measured performance must be comparable to the target workload.

Rule_Description: If the workload's required memory cannot fit on one candidate GPU, additional GPUs may be required, subject to the chosen memory-sharding/parallelism strategy.
Inputs: Required memory; usable memory per GPU; parallelism/sharding strategy
Condition: Required memory > usable memory of one GPU
Output_Decision: Increase GPU count or change candidate/parallelism; then re-evaluate per-GPU memory feasibility
Exact_Source_Title: Parallelism Strategies Guide / existing GPU rules
Page_Section_Table: Tensor Parallelism; FSDP; memory constraints
Evidence: NVIDIA documents TP/FSDP as mechanisms that split/shard model state when a model does not fit.
Applicability: Primarily large-model training; analogous memory-sharding logic only when supported by serving/training framework.
Limitations: Memory division is not automatic; data parallel replication does not reduce model memory per GPU.

Rule_Description: If one GPU is memory-feasible but cannot meet the workload performance target, DSS should evaluate additional GPUs using validated multi-GPU performance evidence.
Inputs: Single-GPU performance; target performance; multi-GPU benchmark/scaling evidence
Condition: Single-GPU performance < target AND validated multi-GPU configuration exists
Output_Decision: Evaluate the smallest validated GPU configuration that satisfies the target
Page_Section_Table: Training time/performance and inference scenario metrics are workload-specific; multi-GPU configurations use explicit parallelism.
Evidence: High
Confidence: Workloads with validated multi-GPU scaling evidence.
Applicability: Do not derive multi-GPU performance by multiplying single-GPU peak FLOPS unless validated.
Limitations: C — requires workload benchmark evidence

Rule_Description: For independently scalable serving units, a preliminary count can be derived from required throughput and validated per-GPU throughput.
Inputs: Required throughput R_req; validated per-GPU throughput R_gpu
Output_Decision: Preliminary throughput capacity lower bound
Hardware_Field: Benchmark throughput; precision-specific performance field where applicable
Page_Section_Table: Concurrency/request-rate modes; throughput measurement
Evidence: Derived from measured serving capacity, not theoretical peak FLOPS.
Applicability: Inference-serving units that can be replicated without changing per-unit workload behavior.
Limitations: Multi-GPU communication/model parallelism can invalidate the simple ratio.

Rule_Name: Compute-Based GPU Count With Validated Effective Performance
Rule_Description: A preliminary training compute count may be estimated when total required work and validated effective performance per GPU are known.
Inputs: Total workload compute W; effective per-GPU performance P_eff; target time T
Output_Decision: Preliminary compute-based GPU lower bound
Hardware_Field: Precision-specific compute field; benchmark-derived effective performance
Page_Section_Table: Training wall-clock target; precision performance evidence
Evidence: Derived engineering relationship; P_eff must be measured/validated for the workload.
Applicability: Training workloads where compute work can be estimated and effective performance is available.
Limitations: Do not substitute theoretical peak FLOPS for P_eff without validation; communication and utilization losses matter.

Rule_Description: When a validated per-GPU training throughput or effective compute rate is available, GPU count can be sized to meet a target training time.
Inputs: Work required W; target time T; effective throughput/performance per GPU S_gpu
Output_Decision: Preliminary minimum count for the target time
Page_Section_Table: Scenarios & Metrics
Evidence: MLPerf explicitly measures wall-clock time to target quality; the count relationship is derived.
Applicability: Training workload with stable scaling evidence.
Limitations: Training work may not scale linearly; use measured scaling efficiency for multi-GPU predictions.

Rule_Name: Single-GPU Baseline Required Before Scaling Efficiency
Rule_Description: When scaling efficiency is evaluated, DSS should retain a validated baseline at a defined GPU count and workload configuration.
Inputs: Baseline GPU count N1; baseline time/performance; workload configuration
Output_Decision: Use baseline as the reference for multi-GPU efficiency
Page_Section_Table: Performance Optimizations / parallelism configurations
Evidence: Scaling comparisons require a defined configuration; NVIDIA documents multi-GPU configurations and communication overlap.
Applicability: Training/LLM scaling studies.
Limitations: A baseline from a different workload or configuration is not valid for the target.

Rule_Description: Scaling efficiency is computed from baseline execution time and N-GPU execution time.
Inputs: Baseline time T1; N-GPU time TN; GPU count N
Output_Decision: Use measured efficiency to avoid assuming linear scaling
Page_Section_Table: Communication Bottlenecks / performance optimizations
Evidence: Formula is derived from the definition of ideal linear strong scaling and measured execution time.
Applicability: Strong scaling with same workload/problem size.
Limitations: Not a universal threshold; DSS must not invent an efficiency cutoff without project approval.

Rule_Name: Use Measured Scaling Efficiency For Multi-GPU Prediction
Rule_Description: Predicted multi-GPU performance should use validated scaling evidence where available rather than assuming ideal linear speedup.
Inputs: Single-GPU performance; multi-GPU performance; scaling efficiency
Output_Decision: Use measured scaling relationship for the selected workload/configuration
Page_Section_Table: NVIDIA documents communication bottlenecks and tradeoffs that can reduce scaling efficiency.
Evidence: High
Applicability: Scaling efficiency depends on topology, communication and workload.
Limitations: A

Rule_Name: Data Parallelism Replicates Model And Splits Batch
Rule_Description: In data parallel training, the model is replicated and the batch is partitioned across data-parallel workers.
Inputs: DP degree; global/micro batch; model state
Output_Decision: Treat DP as batch/work replication; do not count it as model-memory sharding in standard DDP
Page_Section_Table: Data Parallelism / Standard Distributed Data Parallel
Evidence: NVIDIA explicitly states each GPU has a full model copy and processes a portion of the batch in standard DDP.
Applicability: Standard DDP-style training.
Limitations: FSDP/sharded variants change model-state placement; do not apply standard DDP memory behavior to them.

Rule_Description: Tensor parallelism should be considered when model layers do not fit on one GPU or large layers benefit from splitting across GPUs.
Inputs: Model layer memory; TP degree; GPU memory
Condition: Model/layers cannot fit or TP is validated as beneficial
Output_Decision: Use TP to distribute layer computation/memory when supported; validate communication overhead
Hardware_Field: GPU_Count; GPU_Memory; Interconnect field reference only
Page_Section_Table: Tensor Parallelism; Memory Constraints; Communication Bottlenecks
Evidence: NVIDIA documents TP as splitting individual layers and notes communication tradeoffs.
Applicability: Megatron-style model-parallel training.
Limitations: Do not copy topology specs or create compatibility rules here.

Rule_Description: Pipeline parallelism should be considered for very deep models when distributing model depth across GPUs is supported and validated.
Inputs: Model depth; PP degree; pipeline configuration
Output_Decision: Use PP to distribute model depth and re-evaluate efficiency
Page_Section_Table: Pipeline Parallelism; Communication Bottlenecks
Evidence: NVIDIA documents PP as splitting model layers by depth and notes that higher PP can reduce efficiency in some configurations.
Applicability: Deep-model distributed training.
Limitations: Do not infer a universal optimal PP degree.

Rule_Name: Multi-Node Scaling Requires Cross-Node Communication Evidence
Rule_Description: When GPU scaling crosses nodes, DSS should require evidence that the distributed workload remains performance-feasible under the target topology.
Inputs: GPU count; nodes; multi-node benchmark; scaling efficiency; communication configuration
Output_Decision: Use multi-node benchmark/scaling evidence; do not extrapolate single-node results blindly
Hardware_Field: GPU_Count; benchmark performance; Interconnect field only as existing catalogue reference
Page_Section_Table: NVIDIA documents communication bottlenecks and overlap strategies and shows scaling tradeoffs.
Evidence: High
Applicability: Do not introduce network sizing/compatibility rules here.
Limitations: A

Rule_Name: Communication Overhead Must Be Reflected In Scaling Evidence
Rule_Description: If communication becomes material to distributed execution, the scaling evidence used by DSS must reflect that communication rather than compute-only peak performance.
Inputs: Communication time; total time; scaling run; parallelism strategy
Condition: Distributed configuration has communication between GPUs
Output_Decision: Use end-to-end measured performance/scaling rather than compute-only estimates
Page_Section_Table: NVIDIA identifies communication bottlenecks and recommends communication overlap; TP can become communication-limited.
Evidence: High
Applicability: No universal communication overhead percentage is assumed.
Limitations: A

Rule_Description: DSS must preserve observed non-linear scaling behavior and must not replace measured scaling with an ideal linear assumption.
Inputs: Observed speedup; GPU count; baseline performance
Condition: Measured scaling deviates from ideal linear scaling
Output_Decision: Use observed scaling curve/efficiency for subsequent sizing decisions
Page_Section_Table: Communication Bottlenecks / Choosing the Right Strategy
Evidence: NVIDIA explicitly describes communication/performance tradeoffs that affect scaling.
Applicability: Any distributed workload with measured scaling.
Limitations: No universal scaling-efficiency threshold is imposed.

Rule_Name: Throughput And Latency Must Both Be Checked For Latency-Sensitive Inference
Rule_Description: For latency-sensitive inference, a GPU count that satisfies throughput alone is insufficient unless the same configuration also satisfies the latency target.
Inputs: Required throughput; measured throughput; latency target; measured latency; GPU count
Condition: Inference workload has both throughput and latency requirements
Output_Decision: Accept only configurations satisfying both target dimensions
Page_Section_Table: Triton measures latency/throughput at concurrency/request-rate levels; MLPerf Server uses scenario-specific latency-constrained performance.
Evidence: High
Applicability: Exact percentile/latency target remains workload-defined.
Limitations: A

Rule_Name: Redundancy/Standby GPU Count Must Be Project-Defined
Rule_Description: No universal standby GPU factor is established here; any redundancy GPU count must come from an approved availability requirement or project parameter.
Inputs: Required service availability; approved redundancy policy; active GPU count
Condition: Redundancy is explicitly required by project/system availability design
Output_Decision: Apply only the approved project redundancy parameter; otherwise do not add standby GPUs
Exact_Source_Title: MLPerf sources do not establish a universal redundancy factor
Page_Section_Table: The reviewed benchmark/scaling sources measure performance, not a universal DSS availability reserve.
Evidence: High
Confidence: Only after Team/Project A or architecture owner defines availability policy.
Applicability: Must not be invented from benchmark results.
Limitations: P — requires project approval

Rule_Name: GPU Count Is The Maximum Of Independent Resource Constraints
Rule_Description: DSS should retain separate count lower bounds for memory and performance/throughput and select a count that satisfies all applicable constraints, then validate scaling.
Inputs: Memory-based count; compute/throughput-based count; latency constraint; scaling configuration
Output_Decision: Candidate count must satisfy every applicable constraint; final count requires validation of scaling and workload performance
Page_Section_Table: Different constraints govern memory feasibility, measured throughput/latency and distributed scaling; the max-bound composition is a derived DSS decision rule.
Evidence: Medium
Applicability: The max of lower bounds is not sufficient if parallelism/topology changes the per-GPU behavior; final validation is required.
Limitations: C — derived; supervisor approval recommended

Inputs: requests/s, tokens/s, samples/s as applicable; N: GPUs

Inputs: dimensionless ratio

Output_Decision: Any strong-scaling study.
